findings.text: `addToLocal` skips any flag whose name is in `c.parentsPflags`. A local flag that shadows a parent's persistent flag is therefore left out of `LocalFlags()`. For example, if the child defines its own `--verbose` and the parent has a persistent `--verbose`, the child's `LocalFlags()`, usage output and `NonInheritedFlags` omit it. `InheritedFlags` then also skips it because `local` doesn't contain it, so the flag's help is shown nowhere.

The rewrite drops the code that merged the global `flag.CommandLine` (goflags registered through pflag) into the root's persistent flags. `mergePersistentFlags` and `LocalFlags` no longer include those flags. Flags such as `--v` or `--logtostderr` registered with `pflag.CommandLine.AddGoFlagSet` are no longer parsed or listed, and passing one now fails with 'unknown flag'.

`lflags`, `iflags` and `parentsPflags` are cached and only ever added to, never rebuilt. If flags are added to a parent after the first call, or the command is re-parented, stale entries remain. Once a name is in `lflags`, a later persistent flag of the same name on a parent is still reported as local. Entries from an old parent stay in `iflags`.
